text:
For most of the third period at Madison Square Garden, the Rangers were losing a game they were mostly controlling. Then they scored twice in quick succession.

Gabe Perreault opened the scoring at 4:39 of the first, deflecting a play from J.T. Miller and Marcus Pettersson. Philadelphia answered in the second with the oddest goal of the night: Simon Benoit scored on a slap shot that our numbers gave less than a 1% chance of going in, at 10:10. Noel Acciari followed at 12:09, set up by Denver Barkey and Jamie Drysdale, and the Flyers' win chance went from 48% to 69%. The Flyers won the second on expected goals (the quality of the chances), 1.40 to 0.97.

The Rangers took over the third, 1.68 expected goals to 0.76, and Joseph Woll held them off for a while. His best save came on Mika Zibanejad, a 25% chance in the third. Then Pavel Dorofeyev tied it on the power play at 13:52, from Zibanejad and Adam Fox, moving New York from 22% to 57%. At 15:21, Tye Kartye won it on a snap shot from Fox and Oliver Bjorkstrand. That goal took the Rangers from 52% to 89% and was worth 0.37 wins, the most of anyone. Kartye, who was never drafted and worked his way up through the AHL in Coachella Valley, was the first star.

Over the full game the Rangers had the better of it, 3.75 expected goals to 2.80, and deserved to win 57% of replays (the share of replays of every shot a team wins). The shot attempts were almost identical, 54 to 53. Miller created 1.20 expected goals on his own shots without scoring, which is the kind of night that usually evens out. Dylan Garand stopped 23 of 25, about 0.8 goals better than expected.

For Philadelphia, this one hurts because of how it was built: a fluky equalizer, a good second period, and then nothing in the third. Sean Couturier's best chance, a 31% look in the second, missed the net. Fox had two assists on the two goals that won it.
headline: Kartye finishes a late Rangers turnaround
